label: Contact Structures
notes: Open by framing contact geometry as the odd-dimensional cousin of symplectic geometry. Where symplectic manifolds are even-dimensional and carry a closed two-form, contact manifolds live in dimension two-n-plus-one and carry a maximally twisted hyperplane field. Promise the standard example on three-space, the Reeb field, Legendrian fronts, and the link to Huygens.

label: Hyperplane Fields
notes: Explain that a contact structure is first of all a field of hyperplanes, one tangent hyperplane chosen smoothly at every point. Locally it is the kernel of a one-form alpha. The whole story turns on whether such a plane field can be integrated to a foliation, or whether it twists so violently that no integral hypersurface exists anywhere.

label: The Contact Condition
notes: State the non-integrability condition precisely. Alpha wedge the n-th power of d-alpha must be nowhere zero, a volume form on the odd-dimensional manifold. Contrast with Frobenius integrability, where alpha wedge d-alpha vanishes. Stress that the condition is independent of the choice of defining form up to a nonvanishing factor, so the plane field carries it.

label: Standard Example on R^3
notes: Walk through alpha equals dz minus y dx on three-space. At each point the plane annihilates dz minus y dx, so its slope in the z-direction is governed by y. As you move along the x-axis the planes rotate, sweeping past vertical. Emphasize visually that this rotation forbids any surface from staying tangent to all of them.

label: Why No Integral Surface
notes: Make the twisting quantitative. Compute d-alpha equals dx wedge dy, so alpha wedge d-alpha equals dz wedge dx wedge dy, the standard volume form, never zero. By Frobenius this nonvanishing obstructs integrability completely. Any candidate surface tangent to the field along a curve is forced off the field as soon as it tries to extend transversely.

label: The Reeb Vector Field
notes: Introduce the Reeb field as the canonical transverse direction picked out by alpha once alpha is fixed, not just its kernel. It is normalized by alpha of R equals one and by d-alpha contracted with R equals zero. For the standard form R is partial-z. Its flow is the geometric skeleton along which contact dynamics propagates.

label: Legendrian Submanifolds
notes: Define Legendrian submanifolds as integral submanifolds of maximal dimension n, everywhere tangent to the contact planes. They are the largest objects the twisting still permits. In the optics picture a Legendrian curve in the one-jet space projects to a wave front, and its tangency to the planes encodes the slope-position relation of rays.

label: Symplectization and Contactization
notes: Sketch the two bridges to symplectic geometry. Symplectization thickens a contact manifold into a symplectic one a dimension higher, the cone or product carrying d of t-alpha. Contactization runs the other way, adding a fiber coordinate to a symplectic manifold with a chosen primitive. A contact manifold appears as a hypersurface of contact type inside its symplectization.

label: Darboux for Contact Forms
notes: State the contact Darboux theorem: near any point coordinates exist in which alpha becomes dz minus the sum of y-i dx-i. There are no local invariants; every contact structure looks like the standard model nearby. Contrast with the rigidity that appears globally and with the symplectic Darboux normal form it parallels exactly.

label: Huygens and Wave Fronts
notes: Connect to Huygens' principle and geometric optics. A wave front evolves by emitting secondary wavelets whose envelope is the next front. Lifting fronts to Legendrian submanifolds of the contact manifold of contact elements makes this propagation single-valued and smooth even where the front develops caustics. Contact flow is the right language for fronts.

label: Recap
notes: Summarize the through-line. A contact structure is a maximally non-integrable hyperplane field; the contact condition is alpha wedge d-alpha-to-the-n nonzero; the Reeb field is the transverse canonical direction; Legendrian submanifolds are wave fronts; symplectization links the theory to even dimensions; and Huygens' principle is its physical heartbeat. Invite questions on caustics.
